title: Young Olympia Band: Buddy Petit, Mac Lacey and Barbarin joining
summary: Members of the Young Olympia band and how drummers followed one another until Barbarin joined.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: That's, that's, that's many years back. Gee whiz. Um. Now they had some very good bands. I mean, uh, came behind this band like, uh, the Yama Lipi Band. Well, that band was terrific. It was in there. Yeah, that band was really a mess of me. They, they, they was better than those bands. Well, I got, just got through calling. It was in there. It was in there. It was really in there. They had, uh, they had, uh, Simon Marrero on the bass. They had John Marrero on the guitar. They had, uh, one time when I heard them, they had, uh, Jimmy Noon on the clarinet. They had Buddy Petit on the cornet. And they had, uh, uh, Yank, uh, Yank Johnson, which is Buddy Johnson's brother, on the trombone. And they had a wonderful drummer. I still, I still say, he was one of the greatest. Little Mac Lacy. Mac Lacy. Nobody ever met you, Jim. He was a wonderful drummer. Smooth to me. Clean. Clean. Didn't make a whole lot of noise. I mean, it's, was there. Didn't even open spaces. I mean, open spaces he filled in. I mean, it was there. Wonderful beat. Good time. Wonderful band. Wonderful band. One of the greatest bands. And then, after that, in that same band, they had, uh, Bay Shea came with the band for a while. And, uh, uh, they changed, uh, they changed drummers. They had, uh, I know all the pass. And after I know all the pass, they had a, uh, a follower by the name of Rabbit. He came through here with some minstrel show. He was pretty good drummer too. And then, uh, after Rabbit, I think I was the next man to go with the Young Lumpet Band at the time. Mm-hm. on trombone. He had, they had Jean Vigne one time on the drums. And a clarinet player, who was a clarinet player that time? I don't know if it was Piku, I wouldn't say it was Piku. Piku, no. It wasn't Piku. It was a clarinet player. Let's see, George was with Imperial. Big Allah was with Superior. Might have been, might have been Piku, I don't know. Might have been Piku. And, let's see on bass. They had, who was the bass band there, that time. That's beautiful. Well, don't worry about it.
Did you ever hear the... It's a good band though. Yeah. The T.O.s much? On the clarinet?

That's right. That's, that's where the clarinet come in. That was T.O. The Raza Teo. That's the guy. Couldn't call with the old friend of them. That's right. Then they had a guy that played the guitar. He's an old timer. I don't know. And I can't recall his name. I don't know.
Is he here in town? Huh? Is he here in town now? The guitar player.
I think we know his dad is dead. But he died there. He died there, you know.
